summary: Stops accepting work and waits for all accepted factories and tasks to finish.

p: Cancellation only stops this caller's wait; admission remains closed and accepted work remains owned. Each returned task retains its original outcome. A faulted task is logged once (event 1013) without failing the drain; cancellations are not logged. Call again or dispose asynchronously to await completion after a cancelled wait.

When called from accepted work of this scope, including code that inherits its execution context, the drain waits for all other accepted work but not for the calling work, which cannot finish while it awaits its own drain. Work such as "Save and close" can therefore dispose its owner. Code that runs in that work after the drain must not rely on resources the owner releases.

A host that can acknowledge state delivery before the next dependent frame is sent.
remarks: Desktop implements this because its

coalesces snapshots per route, and awaiting script completion lets a slow WebView fall behind into a bounded recovery snapshot. CS-WebUI does not implement it: WebUI's only acknowledged script call answers from one client and blocks a native thread. Its

instead writes to every client synchronously, under WebUI's process-wide send lock, and blocks until each socket write completes or times out. A slow client therefore applies TCP-level back-pressure: the blocked write holds the bridge's delivery queue, which falls back to a recovery snapshot once it is full, and it also delays sends to every other CS-WebUI window. This is not application-level acknowledgement; frames are written in order, not confirmed as applied.

p: The default clears each navigation region the Window's Bridge presents (each

property of its ViewModel), in declaration order, skipping empty ones. A clear asks the departure guard of every entry and of the child regions they own, as any other navigation would. The window closes when every clear commits; a guard that rejects or fails, a cancelled or superseded clear keeps it open with its entries, and the regions after it are not asked. A guard can confirm through a dialog region of the same window, or through a ReactiveUI interaction that a web View of this window answers: the close is the window's own departure, so the one presentation in the window that has mounted a handler for the interaction is asked. Override it to add checks of your own, and call the base method to keep the navigation guards.
